questions.question: What was Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's childhood name?
questions.explanation: He was born as Tyag Mal, the youngest son of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: Tyag Mal was renamed 'Tegh Bahadur' (Mighty of the Sword) for his bravery in which battle?
questions.explanation: His valour in the Battle of Kartarpur against the Mughals earned him the name Tegh Bahadur.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: Who commanded the Mughal force at the Battle of Kartarpur, where Tegh Bahadur Ji showed his bravery?
questions.explanation: The Mughal army at Kartarpur was led by Painda Khan.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: In which village did Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji live in meditation for many years before becoming Guru?
questions.explanation: He lived a contemplative life at Bakala, where Gurdwara Bhora Sahib marks his place of meditation.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: Which merchant revealed Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji as the true Guru at Bakala?
questions.explanation: Bhai Makhan Shah Lubana, fulfilling a vow made when his ship was in danger, found the true Guru and proclaimed 'Guru ladho re'.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: How many gold coins did Makhan Shah Lubana place before each claimant at Bakala?
questions.explanation: He offered two coins to each claimant; only Tegh Bahadur Ji asked for the rest of the coins he had vowed.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
questions.note: Total coins vowed differs by source (500 or 101); only the per-claimant offering is asked.

questions.question: According to tradition, how many false claimants had set themselves up as Guru at Bakala?
questions.explanation: Twenty-two claimants set up seats at Bakala after Guru Har Krishan Ji's passing.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji founded Chak Nanaki in 1665. What is the town known as today?
questions.explanation: Chak Nanaki, founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, grew into Anandpur Sahib.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: Chak Nanaki was named after whom?
options: Mata Nanaki Ji, the Guru's mother
questions.explanation: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji named the town after his mother, Mata Nanaki Ji.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: From whom did Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji obtain the land for Chak Nanaki?
questions.explanation: The land near Makhowal was obtained from Rani Champa of the Kahlur (Bilaspur) state for a token sum.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: Who led the delegation of Kashmiri Pandits that sought Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's protection at Anandpur Sahib?
questions.explanation: In 1675 Pandit Kirpa Ram Datt of Mattan led the Kashmiri Pandits who appealed against forced conversions.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: In which part of Delhi was Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji martyred?
questions.explanation: He was beheaded at Chandni Chowk, where Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib now stands.
questions.source: The Tribune: Sis Ganj and Rakab Ganj Sahib

questions.question: In which year was Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji martyred in Delhi?
questions.explanation: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was martyred in Delhi in November 1675 on Aurangzeb's orders.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: How was Bhai Mati Das martyred at Chandni Chowk?
options: He was boiled in a cauldron
He was wrapped in cotton and burnt
questions.explanation: Bhai Mati Das was sawn apart while reciting Japji Sahib, refusing to give up his faith.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: How was Bhai Sati Das martyred?
options: He was wrapped in cotton and set on fire
questions.explanation: Bhai Sati Das was wrapped in cotton and set alight, remaining steadfast in his faith.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: How was Bhai Dayala martyred?
options: He was placed in a cauldron of boiling water
He was wrapped in cotton and burnt
questions.explanation: Bhai Dayala was boiled in a cauldron while reciting Gurbani.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: Who carried Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's sacred head from Delhi to Anandpur Sahib?
questions.explanation: Bhai Jaita (later Bhai Jiwan Singh) brought the head to Anandpur Sahib, where it was cremated by Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: Bhai Lakhi Shah Vanjara cremated Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's body by setting his own house on fire. Which Gurdwara marks this site?
questions.explanation: Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib, near Parliament House, stands where Lakhi Shah Vanjara's house was burned to cremate the Guru's body.
questions.source: The Tribune: Sis Ganj and Rakab Ganj Sahib

questions.question: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's bani in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji comprises 59 shabads and how many saloks?
questions.explanation: His bani consists of 59 shabads and 57 saloks (Salok Mahalla 9) in 15 raags.
questions.source: Govt of India (Amrit Kaal) 350th Martyrdom exhibition: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji

questions.question: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji is honoured by which title for giving his life to protect others' freedom of faith?
questions.explanation: He is revered as 'Hind di Chadar', the shield of India, for sacrificing his life for religious freedom.
questions.source: The Tribune: Sis Ganj and Rakab Ganj Sahib
